full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the order dated 19-2-2017 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Revision No.220 of 2017 rejecting the application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 summarily thereby upholding the order No.4 of 2012 passed by the Special Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka allowing the prayer of respondent Nos. 3 and 4 for tendering pardon and citing them as approvers. 

 3. As per direction of the High Court Division, the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 were made accused in the instant case. They appeared before the Court and obtained bail. Thereafter, they filed an application under the provision of section 6(2) of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 tendering pardon. In their application it is stated that they are elderly persons. Earlier they were examined as PWs. Thereafter, pursuant to the direction of the High Court Division, they are impleaded as accused. They are husband and wife. Considering circumstances prevailed in the country at the relevant time and in order to save the lives of the other family members, they transferred money in the account of principal accused Gias Uddin Al-Mamun. They expressed their intention to disclose the entire facts in the Court. So, they may be pardoned. 

 5. Then, the principal accused Gias Uddin Al-Mamun filed aforesaid criminal revision under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 in the High Court Division. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order rejected the said criminal revisional application summarily. 

 9. It appears from the impugned order that Special Judge considering prosecution case and others materials on record allowed the prayer for tendering pardon and also allowed this respondent Nos. 3 and 4 as approvers. From the section 6 sub section 2 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, it appears that Special Judge, with a view to obtaining the evidence of any person supposed to have been directly or indirectly concerned in or privy to the offence, may for reasons to be recorded in writing tender pardon to such person on condition of his taking a full and true disclosure of the whole of the circumstances within his knowledge relative to the offence and to every other person concerned, whether as principal or abettor, in the commission thereof and any pardon so tendered shall, for the purposes of sections 339 and 339A of the Code of the Criminal Procedure. An accomplice by accepting a pardon becomes a competent witness and may, as any other witnesses, be examined on oath. As per provision of section 133 of the Evidence Act an accomplice shall be a competent witness.
